name: PetMatchPro
author: PetMatchPro

sections.description:
PetMatchPro is the most complete animal adoption plugin for WordPress. It connects your shelter or rescue website directly to the data management system you already use – so your available animals are always current, always branded, and always working to find forever homes.

Supported Integrations

  • PetPoint / Petango
  • RescueGroups
  • AnimalsFirst

Major Upgrade from 6.4.6 – A Whole New PetMatchPro

If you’re running an older version of PetMatchPro, the 8.x line is a complete leap forward. The plugin has been rewritten on a modern PHP 8.3+ foundation, with dozens of new operator-facing capabilities. Highlights since 6.4.6:

  • Fast Pages That Stay Up – Animal data is cached inside the plugin, so search and profile pages load without waiting on your shelter software. When cached data is due for a refresh, visitors get the saved copy right away and the update runs in the background. If PetPoint, AnimalsFirst, or RescueGroups goes down, your pages keep showing animals from the last good copy (up to 24 hours old) instead of an error.
  • Lightning-Fast Analytics Dashboard – A daily-summary architecture means dashboards that used to time out on busy shelters now load in under a second, no matter how many millions of events you’ve collected. Track impressions, detail views, adoption clicks, conversion funnels, traffic sources, peak engagement times, new vs. returning visitors, and time-to-action – all from a single Analytics tab.
  • Smarter Impression Tracking – Impressions are only counted when a visitor actually dwells on an animal card (500ms minimum), so your numbers reflect real interest, not page-scroll noise. Pages with 300+ animals produce clean, meaningful data, and high-traffic sites stay responsive while it’s collected.
  • Conversion vs. Engagement Split – The dashboard distinguishes adoption-intent actions (adoption application, email, phone, foster, meet-and-greet, donation, sponsor, volunteer) from engagement actions (video plays, shares, directions). Know what’s actually driving placements.
  • Faceted Search Filters – As visitors narrow a search, filter choices that would return no animals are greyed out, so nobody lands on an empty page. Return to Search keeps their filters and sort order.
  • Dynamic Banners – Drive the banner on search cards and detail pages from any animal field (for example “Fee Waived” or “Bonded Pair”), with your own labels and colors.
  • Adopted Animals Handled Gracefully – When an animal is adopted, visitors who follow an old link land on an adoption celebration page with similar animals instead of a dead end. Animals that leave for other reasons show a “No Longer Available” message, and search engines are told to drop the old page.
  • Search-Friendly Profiles – Each animal profile gets one clean set of SEO tags and structured data, even alongside other SEO plugins, and an animal XML sitemap (/pmp-animals.xml) helps search engines find every listing.
  • Visual Shortcode Builder – An admin tab generates correct, copy-paste-ready shortcodes for the partner, method, license tier, installed templates, and field set you’ve configured. No more hand-typing parameters from the documentation.
  • Setup Wizard – A 13-step guided setup walks you through partner selection, method types, field presets, template choices, contact info, filters, labels, colors, and the poster page. Stand up a working configuration in minutes.
  • Hide Empty Fields – A per-method admin toggle (plus a shortcode parameter) suppresses empty fields on both search cards and detail pages. Cleaner layouts for unnamed-intake animals and partial records.
  • Search-Card Hover Text – Standardized, accessible tooltips and ARIA labels on every animal card across all three partners, with method-aware defaults (“Have You Seen {Name}?” for lost, “Help Rehome This {Species}” for found, “Learn More About {Name}” for adopt).
  • Lost & Found Search – Combined lost-and-found search results, partner-aware location handling, and printable lost/found posters with QR codes that route back to the animal’s detail page.
  • Print Posters – One-click adoptable, lost, and found posters with branded layouts, QR codes for last-seen or found locations, and the option to set a dedicated poster page. A Print Posters button on search results prints a whole page of animals at once.
  • Age Your Way – Show ages in years or in years and months, on all three partners.
  • Currency Symbols Worldwide – £, €, and $ render correctly on detail pages, search cards, and posters – regardless of your locale.
  • Modernized Template Library – 60+ search and detail templates across all three partners, including default, hero, conversion, conversion-no-app, profile, navigation, similar-animals, and celebration variants. Theme template overrides are supported (Junior+).
  • Multi-Lingual Ready – Full Spanish (es_ES) translation included; .pot file regenerated from current source for any custom locale.
  • WordPress.org Compliant – Color values validated at save and at render. Unserialize calls hardened against object injection. License-gated UI is hidden rather than shown locked. Operational logs route through a structured logger, with API keys masked, so error_log entries are debuggable in one round-trip.
  • Self-Healing Database – Schema migrations run automatically on the next admin page load after upgrade. No deactivate/reactivate dance.

What PetMatchPro Does for You

Whether you manage a large municipal shelter or a small breed-specific rescue, PetMatchPro gives you the tools to showcase your animals and measure what’s working:

  • Live Animal Listings – Adoptable, found, and lost animals pulled directly from your data management system in real time.
  • Branded Search & Display – Fully customizable search filters, field labels, colors, fonts, and layout so your listings match your website – not a generic widget.
  • Built-In Analytics – Track impressions, detail views, conversion actions, repeat visitors, and time-to-action. Understand what’s actually driving placements.
  • Simple Shortcodes – Place animal search, detail pages, single fields, and admin option values anywhere on your site. Five shortcodes cover every use case.
  • Visual Shortcode Builder – A guided builder generates correct shortcodes for your configuration. No documentation required.
  • Setup Wizard – 13-step guided setup gets you from install to live in minutes.
  • Free to Install – Works out of the box with PetPoint, RescueGroups, or AnimalsFirst – no credit card required to get started.

Why Shelters Choose PetMatchPro

Most shelters rely on an embedded iframe or a redirect to their data system’s generic public portal – giving up control of the visitor experience, losing branding, and getting zero data in return. PetMatchPro keeps visitors on your site, in your brand, and gives you the visibility you need to place more animals.

“PetMatchPro is the missing link between your shelter software and your website.”

Third-party API integrations
PetMatchPro retrieves filter values and species/breed/color lists from AnimalsFirst and RescueGroups APIs on-demand when administrators click the “Refresh Filter Values” button in the plugin’s admin settings. PetMatchPro also retrieves animal records from the configured shelter management system (PetPoint, AnimalsFirst, or RescueGroups) on every public-facing page render. No data is sent off-site without an explicit administrator action; no analytics or telemetry is sent to a vendor-controlled server.
sections.installation:
1. Download the PetMatchPro plugin zip file from petmatchpro.com or your account dashboard.
  2. In your WordPress admin, go to Plugins > Add New > Upload Plugin.
  3. Choose the zip file you downloaded and click Install Now.
  4. Once installed, click Activate Plugin.
  5. In your WordPress admin menu, go to PetMatchPro > Settings to enter your license key and configure your data integration partner (PetPoint, RescueGroups, or AnimalsFirst).
  6. Follow the step-by-step setup wizard to connect your account and configure your search display.
  7. Add the provided shortcodes to any page or post to display your animal listings.

For additional help, visit petmatchpro.com/faq.
sections.faq:
Visit https://petmatchpro.com/faq/ for answers to our most frequently asked questions.

Configuration Constants

PetMatchPro reads a small set of optional define() constants from wp-config.php. These are operator-only kill switches and debugging toggles – none are required for normal operation. Add them above the /* That's all, stop editing! */ line.

  • PMP_ANALYTICS_LEGACY_READS (since 8.9.6) – When defined and truthy, every dashboard read method that was migrated to the daily summary table in 8.9.4 falls back to its pre-8.9.4 raw-events body. Use as a one-line rollback if a migrated dashboard widget shows surprising numbers and you want to compare against the legacy implementation while the operator team investigates.
    Example: define( 'PMP_ANALYTICS_LEGACY_READS', true );
    Equivalent filter (theme functions.php / mu-plugin): add_filter( 'pmp_analytics_legacy_reads', '__return_true' ); – the constant takes precedence when both are set.

  • PMP_PROFILE (since 8.26.0) – When defined as exactly true, turns on the built-in performance profiler for support work. The profiler only runs when all three conditions are met: this constant is true, the person viewing the page can manage options (an administrator), and the URL has ?pmp_profile=1. It then writes coarse request timings (page milestones and one summary line per [pmp-search] render) to the PHP error log only – no page markup, headers, or output change, and the rendered HTML is byte-identical whether it is on or off. A logged-out visitor adding ?pmp_profile=1 never triggers it and never writes to the log. Administrators always fetch live data (they bypass the cache), so the profiler’s fetch time reflects a live call. Leave it undefined on production once you are done; remove the line to turn it off.
    Example: define( 'PMP_PROFILE', true );

  • PMP_CARD_DATA_ALL (since 8.26.0) – When defined and truthy, restores the pre-8.26.0 behavior of emitting every non-empty animal field as a data- attribute on each search card. 8.26.0 trims those attributes to only the ones Pet Match Pro’s own JavaScript reads (filters, sorting, dates, posters), which makes large list pages smaller and faster. Define this only as a one-line rollback if a custom theme or script on your site depended on a card attribute that is no longer emitted, while you update that code.
    Example: define( 'PMP_CARD_DATA_ALL', true );

For the full list with examples, see the wp-config.php Configuration Constants KB article in the docs folder (docs/kb/09-troubleshooting/14-wp-config-constants.html).

Internationalization

PetMatchPro is fully translation-ready and ships with a complete Spanish (es_ES) translation out of the box. Every user-facing string – admin settings, the 13-step setup wizard, public-facing templates, error messages, and all shortcode output – is wrapped in WordPress’s standard translation functions with the pet-match-pro text domain.

What’s included:

  • Full Spanish (es_ES) translation – .po source and compiled .mo files in the plugin’s languages/ directory.
  • Up-to-date .pot template regenerated from the current source. Drop it into Loco Translate, Poedit, or any GlotPress-compatible tool to add your own locale.
  • Locale-aware currency rendering – the pound sign, euro sign, and dollar sign render correctly on detail pages, search cards, and posters regardless of the site language.
  • All five shortcodes ([pmp-search], [pmp-details], [pmp-detail], [pmp-option], [pmp-social-share]) emit translated strings, including hover text, field labels, accessibility labels, and error messages.
  • Method-aware default strings (“Learn More About {Name}”, “Have You Seen {Name}?”, “Help Rehome This {Species}”) are translated, not hardcoded.

Switching languages requires no plugin-side configuration. Change the site language under Settings > General > Site Language and PetMatchPro follows automatically. Custom translations placed in wp-content/languages/plugins/pet-match-pro-{locale}.mo take precedence over the bundled files and survive plugin updates.

If you produce a translation for a locale we don’t yet ship, send the .po file to support@petmatchpro.com and we will consider bundling it in a future release.

upgrade_notice.8.31.0: Reliability release for PetPoint and RescueGroups sites. When PetPoint or RescueGroups is down or slow, pages now keep showing animals from the last good copy (up to 24 hours old) instead of an "Unable to reach animal database" message, including PetPoint lost and found searches. RescueGroups requests now use the same timeout and outage protection as the other partners. No schema or settings change. Safe drop-in upgrade - recommended for all sites.
upgrade_notice.8.30.1: Maintenance release. The cache statistics now show the estimated time saved correctly (for example "1 minute" and "2 hours" instead of "1 minutes" and "2 hours, 0 minutes"), and a PHP deprecation notice from that panel is gone. Also makes background cache refreshes more reliable on AnimalsFirst sites: an API error earlier in the same page request no longer stops a later refresh from saving fresh data. No schema or settings change. Safe drop-in upgrade - recommended for all sites.
upgrade_notice.8.30.0: Performance release. Visitors no longer wait when a cached result is due for a refresh: Pet Match Pro shows the saved copy right away and refreshes it after the page is sent. During a PetPoint, AnimalsFirst or RescueGroups outage, pages that have a saved copy load at normal speed instead of waiting on the partner. No schema or settings change. Safe drop-in upgrade - recommended for all sites.
upgrade_notice.8.29.2: Maintenance release. Fixes a few internal helper methods that referenced undefined settings constants. These methods are not called anywhere today, so there is no visible change for visitors or admins; the fix removes errors that would have surfaced if a future template or add-on called them. No schema or settings change. Safe drop-in upgrade - recommended for all sites.
upgrade_notice.8.29.1: Maintenance release. Fixes an error on the adoption celebration page, introduced in 8.28.1, that could make the page fail to load on AnimalsFirst and PetPoint sites using the celebration (similar-animals) template. Also speeds up AnimalsFirst sites when AnimalsFirst is slow: the filter values that profile and search pages need are now served from Pet Match Pro's cache instead of being fetched live on every pageview, so a slow AnimalsFirst no longer makes every profile wait several seconds. No schema or settings change. Safe drop-in upgrade - recommended for all sites.
upgrade_notice.8.29.0: The animal XML sitemap is fixed and has moved to a new address: /pmp-animals.xml. The old /pmp-sitemap.xml was being claimed by SEO plugins (Yoast, Rank Math, All in One SEO) and returned 404; where Pet Match Pro still receives that old path, it now redirects to the new one. The sitemap also now lists your animals (it was previously empty), includes only the pages search engines should index, carries a last-changed date where your shelter system provides one, and removes duplicate entries. If you submitted the old /pmp-sitemap.xml to Google Search Console, submit the new /pmp-animals.xml URL. robots.txt and the admin SEO diagnostics use the new path automatically, and no Permalinks re-save is needed. No schema or settings change. Recommended for sites with the SEO sitemap enabled.
upgrade_notice.8.28.1: Maintenance release. Fixes dates on animal detail pages. Detail pages now follow your General > Date Format setting on every detail template, not just the default one - so layouts like the navigation, profile, similar-animals, and celebration templates no longer show raw dates (e.g. "2026-09-02") when you have set a different format. This also fixes a day/month swap in the default PetPoint detail template, where a date like Sep 2 could display as "02-09". Separately, the setup wizard file now loads only in the WordPress admin, trimming front-end page load; the wizard and its admin steps are unaffected. No schema or settings change. Safe drop-in upgrade - recommended for all sites, especially PetPoint.
upgrade_notice.8.28.0: Maintenance release. On detail pages, Pet Match Pro now strips a foreign SEO plugin's JSON-LD (application/ld+json) so Google sees only Pet Match Pro's own structured data, not a second WebPage entity pointing at the shell page; developers can turn this off with the new pmp_seo_dedupe_jsonld filter. The Colors tab gains four new Structured template settings: card background, card border, status button text, and status button background (Premium and up). No schema or settings-storage change. Safe drop-in upgrade - recommended for all sites.
upgrade_notice.8.27.1: Maintenance release. On detail pages, Pet Match Pro now emits a single clean set of SEO tags when an SEO plugin (Yoast, Rank Math, All in One SEO, or SEOPress) is also active, so you no longer get duplicate canonical, robots, or Open Graph tags; developers can adjust this with the new pmp_seo_dedupe_head filter. The Success Stories (preferred) detail page now shows a sensible default title. The classic search form no longer renders dropdowns that have no options. Animals that are no longer available carry identifying body classes for easier theming. Minor admin styling and internal cleanups. No schema or settings change. Safe drop-in upgrade - recommended for all sites.
upgrade_notice.8.27.0: Smarter search filters, a working classic search form with client-side features, and clean handling of animals that have left your shelter. Client-side filter dropdowns now grey out options that would return no animals for the current selections, so visitors cannot pick a dead-end combination. The classic (reload) search form now filters correctly when client-side features are on. When an animal is gone, its detail page shows a "No Longer Available" message and returns HTTP 404 (or 410 when that method is set to noindex) so search engines drop the old URL; only adopt animals seen in the last 30 days are sent to your adoption celebration page. Preferred (Success Stories) and list detail pages now return 200 and carry a self-referencing canonical, so Google can index them under their own address. No schema or settings change. Safe drop-in upgrade - recommended for all sites.
upgrade_notice.8.26.0: Makes large animal lists lighter and faster, adds a built-in performance profiler for support, and fixes several search-form and detail-page issues. Each search card now carries only the data it actually needs, so list pages with hundreds of animals send noticeably less HTML (about 46% smaller on a 932-card list). A new administrator-only profiler can be switched on from wp-config to help diagnose slow pages. Fixes: "Return to Search" linked to nothing on some detail templates; a client-side filter with no matches showed a blank page; the poster progress bar showed when it should not; bulk Print Posters produced blank photos and QR codes; the classic search form hid every result when client-side features were off; the sort-field label now reads "Sort By" everywhere; empty Primary/Secondary Breed dropdowns now show "Any"; and the PetPoint classic form's Species choice now actually filters. No schema or settings change. Safe drop-in upgrade - recommended for all sites, especially those with large lists. Your saved labels are untouched.
upgrade_notice.8.25.2: Critical fix for RescueGroups sites. In 8.25.0 and 8.25.1, any RescueGroups page that fetched fresh data instead of using the cache (logged-in administrators, an expired cache, or a site with caching turned off) showed "There has been a critical error on this website." This release fixes that. No schema or settings change. Safe drop-in upgrade - install right away on every RescueGroups site running 8.25.0 or 8.25.1.
upgrade_notice.8.25.1: Makes animal list pages noticeably faster by giving every image Pet Match Pro renders the loading hints that WordPress would otherwise add one by one. On a large combined lost-and-found page (hundreds of animals), WordPress was rewriting the whole page once for every image to add these hints, which added several seconds of server time on top of 8.25.0. Pet Match Pro now writes those hints itself, so WordPress has nothing left to rewrite. Nothing about how your pages look changes. The main photo on a detail page and the single large image on hero templates load right away; all other images (cards, thumbnails, similar-animal grids, posters) load as the visitor scrolls. No schema or settings change. Safe drop-in upgrade - recommended for all sites, especially those with large lists.
upgrade_notice.8.25.0: Makes large animal lists fast and simplifies how PetPoint pages are cached. Big lists - a combined lost-and-found page with hundreds of animals - were too large to cache and so were fetched live on every visit, taking 8 to 11 seconds. Pet Match Pro now compresses its cached animal data, so these lists fit in the cache and load in a few seconds like the smaller ones. Separately, PetPoint now caches the raw data it receives instead of the finished page, matching AnimalsFirst and RescueGroups: label, color, template, and field changes you save now reach visitors immediately instead of waiting for the cache to expire, the same list shown on two different pages now reports clicks to the correct page, and random sort order is no longer frozen. Whole-page caching is left to your host or caching plugin, where it belongs. This release contains everything in 8.24.3. No schema or settings change. Safe drop-in upgrade - recommended for all sites, especially those with large lists. Downgrade note: if you roll back to 8.24.x after installing this, go to Pet Match Pro > Tools > Clear Cache right afterward, because older versions cannot read the new compressed cache rows.
upgrade_notice.8.24.3: Removes the page refresh signal added in 8.24. It was meant to tell your host or caching plugin to refresh pages that show animals when the animal data changed, but the hosts and caching plugins we tested (Kinsta and LiteSpeed Cache) do not listen for it, so it did nothing. If your site uses a page cache, set a short cache time for your animal list pages instead (for example 5 minutes). The upgrade cleans up the small amount of data the signal stored. Navigation and everything else from 8.24 is unchanged. No schema or settings change. Safe drop-in upgrade.
upgrade_notice.8.24.2: Adoption search and profile pages can now be page-cached by your host or caching plugin. Until now, every Pet Match Pro search and profile page started a server session, which tells every host and caching plugin "never cache this page" - so each visit rebuilt the page from scratch, and a busy site could slow to a crawl. The session is gone. Previous / Next, First / Last, "Animal X of Y", and Back to Results work exactly as before on all navigation templates for PetPoint, AnimalsFirst, and RescueGroups, but the visitor's result list is now remembered in their own browser for one hour instead of on your server. Client-side filter and sort no longer call the server at all. When a visitor lands on a profile directly (for example from Google), the navigation bar and Back to Results stay hidden, the same as before. New: when Pet Match Pro's cached animal data actually changes, it sends WordPress's standard "page updated" signal for the pages that show animals, so hosts and caching plugins that refresh on that signal update those pages sooner. Requires the API cache to be on. Custom theme templates that called getReturnToSearchUrl() for their own Back to Results button will no longer show that button - copy the button from a bundled navigation template to restore it. No schema or settings change. Safe drop-in upgrade - recommended for all sites, especially busy ones.
upgrade_notice.8.23.29: Three caching fixes found while investigating a production slowdown. First, PetPoint animal profile pages are now cached. Before this release only PetPoint search results were cached - every profile view fetched the animal live from PetPoint, twice when SEO was enabled, and the Animal Details Cache Duration setting had no effect on PetPoint sites. Profiles now honor that setting, and if PetPoint is briefly unreachable a recently cached profile is shown instead of an error. Second, RescueGroups profile pages now use the Animal Details Cache Duration setting (they were using the search duration), and logged-in administrators and any page loaded with ?pmp_nocache=1 now see live RescueGroups data, matching PetPoint and AnimalsFirst. On all three partners an adopted or removed animal is never cached. Third, opening any wp-admin page no longer empties the site's entire object cache (Redis or Memcached). The plugin was clearing all of it on every admin page and every admin-ajax request, which slowed the whole site for every visitor on hosts with a persistent object cache. No schema, settings, or migration change. Safe drop-in upgrade - recommended for all sites.
upgrade_notice.8.23.28: Two fixes from a production slowdown. First, AnimalsFirst animal profile pages are now cached. Before this release only AnimalsFirst search results were cached - every profile view fetched the animal live from AnimalsFirst, often twice when SEO was enabled, and the Animal Details Cache Duration setting had no effect on AnimalsFirst sites. Profiles now honor that setting. Logged-in administrators and any page loaded with ?pmp_nocache=1 still see live data, and an adopted or removed animal is never cached. Second, the license check can no longer hang a wp-admin page. When the saved license answer is due for re-validation, the page loads immediately with the saved answer and the check runs in the background. License server calls now time out after 30 seconds (15 in the background) instead of 120, and if the license server is unreachable a previously valid license keeps working for about 72 hours instead of about 3. No schema, settings, or migration change. Safe drop-in upgrade - recommended for AnimalsFirst sites.
upgrade_notice.8.23.27: Stops partner API credentials from being written to the server error log. When an AnimalsFirst request failed and the plugin fell back to its cached copy, the warning it logged included the full request URL - and AnimalsFirst carries its API token in that URL, so the live token ended up in the host's error log, readable by anyone with hosting-panel access. Every plugin log line now masks credential values in URLs (api_token, authKey, and similar) as [REDACTED]. Nothing else about logging changes: the same warnings still appear, with the same detail. If your site has logged AnimalsFirst fallback warnings in the past, consider asking AnimalsFirst to rotate your API token. No schema, settings, or migration change. Safe drop-in upgrade.
upgrade_notice.8.23.26: The four size parameters now actually work. icon_size, title_size, subtitle_size, and banner_size were accepted by the shortcodes, gated by license tier, and documented in the admin and the knowledge base - but had no effect on any page, on either search or detail. The code that turned them into CSS was never called. If you set one of these in the past and concluded it did nothing, you were right. All four now apply on both [pmp-search] and [pmp-details], scoped to the individual shortcode, so two blocks on the same page can size differently. icon_size accepts small/large/xl or a whole number from 8 to 200; values outside that range, or with units attached ("48px"), are ignored rather than guessed at. Because these parameters previously did nothing, any page already carrying one will change appearance after upgrading - worth a quick look at pages using them. Pages without them render exactly as before. No schema, settings, or migration change. Safe drop-in upgrade.
upgrade_notice.8.23.25: Fixes Dynamic Banners not appearing on detail pages. If your banner source field was not also a field your detail page displays - Memo List is the common case - the banner showed correctly on search result cards and then silently disappeared on the animal's detail page, with nothing in the settings to explain why. The source field is now always available to the banner logic on detail pages regardless of which fields that page displays. Two related fixes: banners built on a field whose name differs between search and detail data (PetPoint Type/Found Type, Name) now resolve on both; and a source field that returns a list rather than a single value - again, Memo List - now matches on any entry in the list, not just the first. If a fallback banner was masking the problem, you may now see real banners where a blank strip used to be. Worth checking: a Default / Fallback row with a background color but no text color renders white-on-white and looks like no banner at all. No schema, settings, or migration change. Safe drop-in upgrade - recommended for any site using Dynamic Banners.
upgrade_notice.8.23.24: The banner parameter now works on [pmp-details]. Previously banner="..." was accepted on [pmp-search] only, so the same copy showed on a search result card and then silently disappeared on the animal's detail page - with no error and nothing in the settings to explain it. Set banner="..." on [pmp-details] and it renders as a strip above the main photo, using the same precedence as a search card: static copy wins over Dynamic Banners and shows even when the per-method "Show on detail pages" toggle is off. A companion banner_size parameter (small, large, xl) scales the detail strip and applies to static and dynamic banners alike. Existing pages are unaffected: with no banner parameter set, detail pages render exactly as before. Premium tier and above. No schema, settings, or migration change. Safe drop-in upgrade.
upgrade_notice.8.23.23: Hardening fix for license validation. If the license server was unreachable or returned an unexpected response, the plugin could crash the WordPress admin with a fatal PHP error instead of reporting the problem. It could also clear a valid, paid license and silently drop the site to free-tier features. Both are fixed: a license-server failure now shows a plain "License Server Unavailable" notice, keeps your saved license in place, and retries automatically. Sites that saw the fatal error will recover on upgrade. No schema, settings, or migration change. Safe drop-in upgrade - recommended for all sites.
upgrade_notice.8.23.22: Age Display can now show ages as years and months, not just years. In General > Display Options > Formatting, when age conversion is enabled, a new Age Format selector chooses "Years only" (e.g. 2 Years) or "Years and months" (e.g. 2 Years 3 Months). Animals under a year still show months, and exact years never show a trailing "0 Months". Applies site-wide across PetPoint, AnimalsFirst, and RescueGroups. Note: the years-only calculation changed from nearest-year rounding to whole-year truncation (a 2-year-8-month animal now reads "2 Years" instead of "3 Years") so both modes agree; the SEO/social title's age reads the same way ("2-Year-Old" instead of "3-Year-Old"). No schema or migration change. Safe drop-in upgrade.
upgrade_notice.8.23.21: Per-animal labels now work on combination (lost + found) search result cards, not just detail pages. Previously, on a combined lost/found search with per-animal labels enabled, every card used the page's method for its labels - so a lost animal could show a "Found Date" heading (and vice versa). Each card now labels itself according to its own type, so lost animals show lost labels and found animals show found labels. Applies to AnimalsFirst across its search layouts and brings the PetPoint structured layout in line with the standard layout (which already did this). Single-method searches are unchanged. No schema, settings, or migration change. Safe drop-in upgrade.
upgrade_notice.8.23.20: Label consistency fix for the AnimalsFirst and RescueGroups detail "navigation" templates. The field labels on those detail pages (and their similar-grid variants) now resolve the same way as everywhere else in the plugin, so a field labels consistently across all three services. Standard and custom labels are unchanged for typical setups; two narrow cases may differ slightly and are worth a look after upgrading: (1) an AnimalsFirst site that set a Search Result label but left the Detail label blank for a field - that field now uses its Detail label / default rather than borrowing the Search Result one; (2) a handful of non-standard fields may show a cleaned-up version of the field name instead of a hardcoded caption. No schema, settings, or migration change. Safe drop-in upgrade.
upgrade_notice.8.23.19: Label consistency fix for the "similar animals" grids. The related-animal grid shown on the celebration/similar detail templates (all three services) now labels its fields exactly the same way as a regular search page, using the same label source as everywhere else in the plugin. Previously those grids used an older label lookup that skipped the built-in default labels, so a field could show a slightly different (or run-together) heading there than on a normal search card. Custom labels you set are honored as before; standard labels are unchanged or improved. No schema, settings, or migration change. Safe drop-in upgrade.
upgrade_notice.8.23.18: Completes the Unified Label Resolver work (D6c, final phase). The "Order By" and "Sort" headings above the search sort controls now resolve their label the same way every other field label does, so a custom label you set for the sort field is honored consistently, and the standard headings are unchanged. The only intentional change: for "featured" search pages, these sort headings (and filter headings) now read from your adopt labels instead of a separate featured slot that was never actually saved, so a custom adopt label now shows through on featured pages too. Dropdown option values are unaffected. No schema, settings, or migration change. Safe drop-in upgrade.
upgrade_notice.8.23.17.1: Two small template display fixes found in testing. 1) On the "wide" and "3-column" detail layouts (including their related-animal "similar" variants), the main photo now sits flush beneath the status banner strip instead of showing rounded top corners. 2) The bulk "Print Posters" button that appears below the related-animal grid on a detail page now loads its styling and click behavior, matching the button on a regular search page. CSS and asset-loading only - no schema, settings, or migration change. Safe drop-in upgrade.
upgrade_notice.8.23.17: Completes the search filter dropdown heading consistency fix (Unified Label Resolver, D6 part 2). The structured-layout filter bar now uses the same label source as every other template, so filter headings are consistent across all layouts and all three services. Standard filters look identical to before; the only headings that change are for non-standard fields you may have added to a filter that do not have a built-in filter label, which now read as a cleaned-up version of the field name. Custom filter labels you set are unchanged, and dropdown option values are unaffected. No schema, settings, or migration change. Safe drop-in upgrade.
upgrade_notice.8.23.16: Consistency fix for search filter dropdown headings (Unified Label Resolver, D6 part 1). The heading above each filter dropdown now uses the same label source as the rest of the plugin, which means multi-word filter fields that previously showed a run-together heading (e.g. "Agegroup") now show the proper built-in label ("Age Group"). Any custom filter label you have set is unchanged, and this affects only the field heading - the dropdown option values are unaffected. Applies to the standard filter bar; the structured-layout filter bar follows in the next update. No schema, settings, or migration change. Safe drop-in upgrade.
upgrade_notice.8.23.15: Small refinement to the last-resort label formatter added in 8.23.14. When a field label has to be generated from the field key (no custom label and no built-in default - only happens for a mistyped or unknown field name in a shortcode), the formatter now also splits camelCase, so "ageGroup" reads "Age Group" (in addition to the underscore/dash handling from 8.23.14). Standard fields are unaffected because they already have proper labels. No schema, settings, or migration change. Safe drop-in upgrade.
upgrade_notice.8.23.14: Consistency update (Unified Label Resolver, DETAIL phase D5, part 3 + humanizer unification). When a field label falls all the way back to being generated from the field key (no custom label and no built-in default), the plugin now uses a single shared formatter everywhere: underscores and dashes become spaces and each word is capitalized (so "spay_neuter" reads "Spay Neuter"). This replaces an older formatter that could leave underscores in place. Standard fields are unaffected because they already have proper labels; this only changes the last-resort formatting of otherwise-unlabeled keys. The one edge case: a hand-typed mixed-case field key in a shortcode (e.g. "ageGroup") is now capitalized as "Agegroup" rather than "Age Group" - stored field keys are lowercase, so normal setups never hit this. No schema, settings, or migration change. Safe drop-in upgrade.
upgrade_notice.8.23.13: Internal maintenance (Unified Label Resolver, DETAIL phase D5, part 2). Removes two dead, unused private helper methods (getLabelValue) left over in the PetPoint and AnimalsFirst detail-function classes after earlier label-resolver phases moved all label resolution onto the shared resolver. No functional change - nothing called these methods. Safe drop-in upgrade.
upgrade_notice.8.23.12: Internal consistency update (Unified Label Resolver, DETAIL phase D5, part 1). The two PetPoint "navigation" detail templates now resolve their field labels through the same shared resolver as every other detail template, instead of each keeping its own private label-lookup chain. For standard detail fields your labels are unchanged; the only visible difference is on fields that previously fell back through search-result / filter labels or needed the PetPoint detail field aliases, which now resolve consistently. No schema, settings, or migration change. Safe drop-in upgrade.
upgrade_notice.8.23.11: Fixes a layout bug on the AnimalsFirst navigation detail templates where the animal detail card could render in the wrong position on the page - jumping above other content (such as a header or hero placed above the shortcode) and pushing that content to the bottom. The two AnimalsFirst navigation templates now buffer their output like every other detail template, so the card renders exactly where the shortcode is placed. Only affects AnimalsFirst "navigation" and "navigation-similar" detail templates. No schema, settings, or migration change. Safe drop-in upgrade.
upgrade_notice.8.23.10: Routes the internal detail label map (used by the navigation-style detail templates on PetPoint and AnimalsFirst) through the unified resolver. Which fields appear is unchanged; only the label text is now resolved consistently - a field with a custom label is unchanged, and a field with no custom label now shows its proper default (or a readable humanized name) instead of, in rare cases, "Not Defined" as a label. Most affects the AnimalsFirst navigation detail template. Verify your PetPoint and AnimalsFirst detail pages (especially navigation templates) after updating. No schema, settings, or migration change. Safe drop-in upgrade.
upgrade_notice.8.23.9: Extends detail-page label standardization to PetPoint. PetPoint animal detail pages and posters now resolve field labels through the unified resolver, reading your Detail labels (and detail defaults) exactly as before. On real data this renders identically; two small improvements come along: a field with no custom label and no built-in default now shows a readable label instead of a placeholder, and short field names used in a detail shortcode (for example the spay/neuter or found/lost location fields) now map to the correct detail label. Your custom labels and the PetPoint lost/found combination search are unchanged. No schema, settings, or migration change. Safe drop-in upgrade.
upgrade_notice.8.23.8: Extends detail-page label standardization to AnimalsFirst. AnimalsFirst animal detail pages and posters now resolve field labels through the unified resolver, reading your Detail labels (and detail defaults) exactly as before. On real data this renders identically; the one visible improvement is that a field with no custom label and no built-in default now shows a readable label instead of a placeholder. Your custom labels and the lost/found per-animal label feature are unchanged. No schema, settings, or migration change. Safe drop-in upgrade.
upgrade_notice.8.23.7: Begins detail-page label standardization, starting with RescueGroups. RescueGroups animal detail pages and posters now resolve field labels through the same unified resolver used for search, reading your shared Search/Detail Result labels. On real data this renders identically to before; the one visible improvement is that a field with no custom label and no built-in default now shows a readable label (for example "Coat Length") instead of a blank. Your custom labels are unchanged. No schema, settings, or migration change. Safe drop-in upgrade.
upgrade_notice.8.23.6: Completes search label standardization for AnimalsFirst and RescueGroups. The AnimalsFirst structured search template and all RescueGroups search templates now resolve field labels from your Search Result labels (and search-result defaults), the same as every other search template, instead of reading Detail labels. IMPORTANT: if you previously customized labels for these cards under the Detail labels, set them under the Search Result labels instead. Review your AnimalsFirst structured and RescueGroups search pages after updating. No schema, settings, or migration change.
upgrade_notice.8.23.5: Routes the PetPoint structured search template's field labels through the unified label resolver, matching the other PetPoint and AnimalsFirst search templates. On real data this renders identically to before; it removes the last per-template search-label path so all single-method search cards resolve labels the same way. No schema, settings, or migration change. Safe drop-in upgrade.
upgrade_notice.8.23.4.1: Minor CSS fix for the PetPoint navigation detail template: the action buttons (Adopt Me, Sponsor Me, etc.) now match the Return to Search button's size and shape on mobile and desktop, instead of stretching wider. No functional change. Safe drop-in upgrade.
upgrade_notice.8.23.4: Extends the unified label system to AnimalsFirst single-method search results (Adopt/Lost/Found/Preferred and Featured cards). Like the PetPoint change in 8.23.2, fields you have not given a custom label now show the proper default label (for example "Age Group" instead of "Age_group") on AnimalsFirst search cards, matching how PetPoint already behaves. Your custom labels are unchanged. No schema, settings, or migration change. Safe drop-in upgrade.
upgrade_notice.8.23.3: Fixes a bug where updating the plugin could reset your custom search button, sort button, and other colors to the defaults. The generated color stylesheet now automatically regenerates from your saved Colors settings after every update, so your colors survive upgrades. If you were affected, this release restores your colors automatically on the next page load (no need to re-save). Safe drop-in upgrade.
upgrade_notice.8.23.2: Phase 2 of the unified label system: PetPoint combined lost & found search results now resolve field labels the same way single-method (Adopt/Lost/Found) search results already do. If you use lost & found labeling, fields you have not given a custom label now show the proper default label (for example "Age Group" instead of "Agegroup") on combination cards, matching your single-method pages. Your custom labels and the per-animal lost/found labeling are unchanged. No schema, settings, or migration change. Safe drop-in upgrade.
upgrade_notice.8.23.1: Phase 1 of the unified label system: PetPoint single-method search results (Adopt, Lost, Found, and Featured cards) now resolve their field labels through the new central resolver instead of per-template code. This is a no-visible-change refactor - your labels render exactly as before - that removes duplicated logic ahead of later improvements. No schema, settings, or migration change. Safe drop-in upgrade.
upgrade_notice.8.23.0: Internal foundation for a unified field-label system (Phase 0 of a multi-phase effort). Adds a single label resolver that will, over the next releases, make every field resolve the same label everywhere - search and detail, every method, every partner. This release only adds the resolver; nothing calls it yet, so there is no visible change. No schema, settings, or migration change. Safe drop-in upgrade.
upgrade_notice.8.22.0: Adds the Featured field as a configurable Search Result label for PetPoint adoptable animals (Premium), so you can rename it under Labels > Adoptable > Search Result Labels the same way you already can on detail pages. Also fixes three display issues: PetPoint Lost and Found search cards now honor their own custom Search Result labels instead of falling back to the Adoptable labels; AnimalsFirst Preferred detail pages now apply your Preferred field labels, field-level licensing, and hide-empty settings (they were collapsing to Adoptable) and no longer error when no Preferred detail template is configured (they fall back to the universal detail layout); and a license-gating fix so search cards rendered through the shared template logic show the correct fields for each tier. No schema, settings, or migration change. Safe drop-in upgrade.
upgrade_notice.8.21.0: Adds a "Print Posters" button to search results ([pmp-search]) that prints a poster for every animal on the current results page, one per page, using your configured poster template. Enable it per method under General > Display Options > Poster Print, or per shortcode with poster_print="true". The Adopt poster is free; Lost, Found, and Preferred posters require Junior tier or higher (same as the existing poster templates). Bulk printing does not record analytics detail-page views. No schema, settings, or migration change. Safe drop-in upgrade.
upgrade_notice.8.20.0: Dynamic Banners now render on single-animal detail pages, as a full-width status strip above the main photo, controlled by a new independent per-method toggle (General > Display > Dynamic Banners > "Show on detail pages"). Detail banners reuse the exact same value mapping, cascade levels, default, and per-value colors as your search-card banners, so one configuration drives both surfaces. The existing enable checkbox is now labeled "Show on search results"; the two toggles are independent, and the detail toggle is OFF by default, so existing sites see no change on detail pages until you opt in. Search grids that mix banner and no-banner cards now keep their photo tops aligned (banner-less cards reserve the banner's height only when the grid actually has a banner). The Analytics "Top Clicked Animals" card is relabeled "Top Viewed Animals" (column "Clicks" -> "Views") to accurately describe that it reports detail-page views. No schema, settings, or migration change. Safe drop-in upgrade.
upgrade_notice.8.19.1: Adds a "New vs Returning Visitors" card to the Analytics dashboard showing new and returning visitor counts and their conversion rates. When the "Track Returning Visitors (cross-day)" setting (added in 8.19.0) is off, the card shows new visitors with returning at 0 plus a note explaining how to enable cross-day returning detection. No schema change. Safe drop-in upgrade.
upgrade_notice.8.19.0: True cross-day returning-visitor analytics, OFF by default. When enabled (Analytics > Tracking Settings > "Track Returning Visitors"), the plugin stores a first-party pmp_visitor_id cookie - an opaque random id, no personal data, never sold or shared, 400-day lifetime - so genuine new-vs-returning visitors can be counted across days instead of the same-day estimate. The widget keeps showing the same-day metric with a "history building" note until about 30 days of history accumulate, then flips automatically. Add a line to your privacy policy if you turn it on (ready-to-paste copy is in the Privacy and Data Retention KB article). Operators with EU traffic can gate the cookie via the pmp_visitor_marker_suppress filter. Additive, forward-only, no data loss. Safe drop-in upgrade.
upgrade_notice.8.18.3: Client-side filtering fix for custom filter groups that relabel a blank/empty field value. When a Primary Field has only "Yes" and blank as values (for example PetPoint good-with-cats/good-with-dogs) and the group's "Other" label surfaces the blank value as a readable option (for example "OK with"), the filter dropdown showed the option but selecting it returned no animals. The matching result cards carried no data attribute for that field, so the option value and the card disagreed and nothing matched. Blank-valued cards now resolve through the same path the dropdown uses, so the option and the card always agree. Centralized in the shared search-template logic, so it applies to every search template across all three partners. No new settings. Non-blank values (including relabeled ones) are unaffected. Safe drop-in upgrade.
upgrade_notice.8.17.2.2: CSS-only hotfix for sites whose theme or page builder sets a global link-accent color (most visibly Elementor). The search sort buttons and detail action buttons could ignore their configured Pet Match Pro colors and show the theme accent instead. Fixed by giving those button color rules higher CSS specificity so they win without !important. If buttons still show the old color after updating, re-save the Colors tab and clear your page cache. No new settings. Safe drop-in upgrade.
upgrade_notice.8.17.2.1: Hotfix found during 8.17 load testing: impression beacons with a double-quote or backslash in a field (for example an animal name like Bob "Buddy") could be silently dropped, because both ingest paths over-stripped the JSON payload. No new settings. Safe drop-in upgrade.
upgrade_notice.8.17.2: Extends the new Hero search layout (Premium/Preferred) to PetPoint and AnimalsFirst, so all three partners can feature a single animal in a homepage hero or banner image zone. PetPoint and AnimalsFirst use template="featured-search-hero" and show your featured-flagged animals (RescueGroups uses template="adopt-search-hero" from 8.17.1). Same behavior on every partner: a full-bleed photo with the animal's name and a "Meet Me" button, a different animal shown at random on each page load, drawn from the filters you already use (species, breed, sex) with count setting the pool size. Also hardens the hero stylesheet so the image always fills its zone regardless of theme grid styles. Free-tier sites fall back to your configured template. Safe drop-in upgrade.
upgrade_notice.8.17.1: New Hero search template (Premium/Preferred) for RescueGroups. Feature one adoptable animal in a homepage hero or banner image zone: a full-bleed pet photo with the animal's name and a "Meet Me" button that links to its detail page. A different animal is shown at random on each page load, drawn from the filters you already use (species, breed, sex), with the count parameter setting the pool size - so no new settings to learn. Add it with one shortcode: [pmp-search type="adopt" template="adopt-search-hero" count="8" pagination="disable" filter="disable" species="cat"]. PetPoint and AnimalsFirst hero variants follow in 8.17.2. Free-tier sites fall back to your configured template. Safe drop-in upgrade.
upgrade_notice.8.16.2.1: Recommended update for 8.16.2 (Dynamic SEO Titles). Fixes the SEO title age on PetPoint detail pages: animals with an unknown age no longer show a wildly wrong value (e.g. "126-Year-Old") - the age is now omitted when unknown, and when shown it rounds to match the age on your search cards and detail pages. Also fixes a problem where a slow or unreachable shelter API could redirect a live, adoptable animal to the adoption celebration page, and resolves a PHP error that could blank a detail page when an API response failed to parse. Safe drop-in upgrade.
upgrade_notice.8.16.2: New Dynamic SEO Titles (Preferred license): animal detail pages now render a keyword-rich, per-animal browser/SEO title - for example "Buddy - 2-Year-Old Rescue Dog for Adoption in Clermont County, Ohio". Set a template per method type (Adopt, Lost, Found, List, Preferred) using tokens for name, age, species, breed, location, and shelter, plus a global Shelter Location for adoptable animals. The title now works with Yoast, Rank Math, All in One SEO, and SEOPress (it previously did nothing on sites running an SEO plugin) and also improves Facebook/X/LinkedIn share cards. Configure it under PetMatchPro Options - Analytics - SEO Settings. Safe drop-in upgrade.
upgrade_notice.8.16.1.1: Refinement of the 8.16.1 Dynamic Banners feature: the settings now live under PetMatchPro Options - General - Display - Dynamic Banners (a collapsible group) instead of a separate tab, source fields are now correct per method type (Lost/Found no longer show Adopt-only fields), a configured banner border now renders, and you can set a per-value text shadow. No change to how banners display on your site. Safe drop-in upgrade.
upgrade_notice.8.16.1: New Dynamic Banners feature (Junior license or higher): drive the search-result banner text and per-value color from an animal field instead of a single static string - for example, show a red "On Hold" banner when PetPoint onhold = Yes and a green "Adopt Me" otherwise. Configure it under PetMatchPro Options - Banners. Also de-importants the banner color CSS (now container-scoped specificity). Search cards only in this release; existing static banner= shortcodes are unchanged. Safe drop-in upgrade.
upgrade_notice.8.16.0.1: Hotfix for AnimalsFirst conversion-button email/phone routing. Foster detection now uses the same primary/fallback + exclusion + label engine as location display, so an animal whose location resolves through your filters (e.g. a site-primary offsite/cafe value) no longer mis-routes the "Ask Us" button to the Adopt Foster contact. No schema change, no operator action - safe drop-in upgrade.
upgrade_notice.8.11.5: WordPress 7.0 compatibility release. Bumped "Tested up to" to 7.0 and "Requires PHP" to 8.3 to align with WordPress 7.0's recommended PHP version. No functional changes - safe drop-in upgrade for any site already on PHP 8.3 or higher. Sites still on PHP 8.1 / 8.2 should upgrade PHP before installing 8.11.5; the plugin will not activate on older PHP and a clear admin notice explains why.
upgrade_notice.MAJOR UPGRADE NOTICE FROM 6.4.6: The 8.x line is a complete modernization. Highlights: lightning-fast analytics dashboard, dwell-time impression tracking, conversion vs. engagement insights, visual Shortcode Builder, 13-step setup wizard, hide-empty-fields toggle, lost & found search with QR-coded posters, standardized hover text, currency-symbol fixes, 60+ modernized templates, Spanish translation, hardened security, and self-healing schema migrations. No deactivate/reactivate needed - the database self-migrates on the next admin page load. See the Description tab for the full "What's New Since 6.4.6" rundown.
upgrade_notice.8.11.3: Second hotfix for the universal-details-default templates. 8.11.2 resolved a fatal but the lost / found URL routes still rendered the adopt layout. Root cause: the template read $_GET['method'] for method detection, which is unreliable under Divi's block-rendering pipeline. Fixed by reading the in-scope $methodType local set by outputDetails() right before the template is required - that value is the canonical method type and survives every rendering path (Divi loops, MultiView, legacy query-string URLs, pretty permalinks). Lost / found / preferred URLs now render the correct layout. No schema change, no operator action.
upgrade_notice.8.11.2: Hotfix for 8.11.1. The new universal-details-default templates fataled on the first page hit with "Typed property must not be accessed before initialization." Root cause: the anonymous template class assigned $this->resolvedMethod after parent::__construct(), but the parent constructor reads that property during loadFieldLevels(). Property assignment is now moved before parent::__construct() in both PetPoint and AnimalsFirst versions. No schema change, no operator action - the auto-flush from 8.10.1.5 still fires on the version bump.
upgrade_notice.8.11.1: New free-tier detail template "universal-details-default" for PetPoint and AnimalsFirst. One method-aware template that renders the adopt, lost, or found layout based on the URL method - so a single template choice covers all method types instead of having to pick adopt-default, lost-default, or found-default per method. AnimalsFirst preferred animals (type=other/outcome/foster/stray/rehome/pending/all) finally have a simple default detail template instead of having to configure the heavy universal-details-navigation. Pick it under General > Templates > Detail Template, or pass via shortcode template parameter. No schema change, no operator action required.
upgrade_notice.8.11.0: Free-tier performance feature: PMP now injects a tag into the head of pages that render PMP shortcodes, warming up the browser's TCP+TLS connection to your partner's animal-photo CDN before the first image is requested. Typical savings: 100-300ms on the first photo load, more on mobile. Detects PMP pages automatically (shortcode in post body OR pretty-permalink detail URL); other pages on your site are unaffected. Default on for new and upgraded installs. Toggle in General > Performance > Preconnect to Partner Photo CDN. See the KB article "Preconnect to Your Partner Photo CDN" for details. No schema change, no operator action required.
upgrade_notice.8.10.1.5: Pretty-permalink fix for AnimalsFirst Preferred animals. The /pmp/{method}/... URL rewrite was hardcoded to adopt|lost|found, so links from a "preferred" search (e.g., type="other", type="outcome", type="foster") landed on a WordPress 404. Regex now also matches "preferred". Rewrite rules now auto-flush on the first request after any version change, so this fix - and every future rewrite-rule change - applies without an operator visiting Settings > Permalinks. No operator action required.
upgrade_notice.8.10.1.4: MAJOR UPGRADE from 6.x: The 8.x line is a full modernization - new analytics dashboard, Shortcode Builder, 13-step setup wizard, lost & found with QR posters, 60+ modernized templates, Spanish translation, and self-healing schema migrations. No deactivate/reactivate needed; the database migrates itself on the next admin page load. Back up your site first. See the Description tab for the full rundown.
upgrade_notice.8.10.1.3: WP.org SVN compatibility fix. Converted a trait-level const to a private static method so the WP.org pre-commit PHP lint (PHP < 8.2) accepts the commit. No runtime behavior change, no schema change, no operator action required.
upgrade_notice.8.10.1.2: Three operator-facing fixes from partner testing. (1) PetPoint XML-parse failure logs now include the actual libxml error messages and a 500-char response body snippet, so a failed animal detail fetch is debuggable in one round-trip instead of guesswork. (2) Recurring "Array to string conversion" PHP warning eliminated from the foster-location check when a partner returns an empty or nested location field. (3) AnimalsFirst lost_found combo search now correctly honors the admin-configured field list under the resolved Found (or Lost) method - "type" and "intake_type" admin checkboxes now display on the cards as expected. No schema change. No operator action required.
upgrade_notice.8.10.1.1: Three template polish fixes. PetPoint adopt-details-navigation-similar now honors admin-configured location labels and currency symbols on every render path. Six AF and RG side-by-side detail templates now correctly stack thumbnails and videos in a single right-side column so videos no longer push the main image off the page. No operator action required.
upgrade_notice.8.10.1: Quality-pass cleanup: removed 59 leftover debug log entries (cleaner PHP error log), tightened analytics SQL identifier quoting for future-proofing, and refreshed the translation source inventory for the upcoming i18n release. No schema change, no UI change, no operator action required.
upgrade_notice.8.10.0: WP.org compliance and security release. Color values are now validated at save and at render (blocks CSS injection). License unserialize paths hardened against object injection. Broken API keys now produce actionable "Authentication Error" hints instead of misleading parse errors. Two free-tier features (THUMBS shortcode param, Poster Details Page) corrected from Premium-only. No operator action required.
upgrade_notice.8.9.10: Three analytics dashboard fixes. (1) Action-click events on slug-style URLs and custom theme templates now capture the animal ID correctly - Conversions by Traffic Source and similar widgets now report real numbers instead of zero. (2) New conversion-vs-engagement split: adoption-intent actions (email, phone, application, foster, donation, etc.) are counted as conversions; engagement actions (video plays, shares, directions) are reported separately. (3) Session ID cookie now persists across navigation so detail-view and action-click events join correctly. Expect more accurate dashboards from 8.9.10 forward.
upgrade_notice.8.9.0 - 8.9.10 (Analytics Performance Ov: A nine-fix series that rebuilt the analytics read path. The dashboard now reads from a pre-aggregated daily summary table instead of grouping millions of raw events on every render. Widgets load lazily as you scroll, results are cached for 60 seconds, and a chunked Rebuild Daily Summaries button repopulates historical data. Sites that used to time out the Analytics tab now load in under a second. After upgrading, click Tools > "Rebuild Daily Summaries" to backfill historical data. No deactivate/reactivate required - schema self-migrates on the next admin page load.
upgrade_notice.8.8.0 / 8.8.0.1: Standardized search-card hover text across all three partners. Animal name, photo, and image links now share consistent, accessible tooltips with ARIA labels for screen readers. Method-aware defaults: "Learn More About {Name}" (adopt), "Have You Seen {Name}?" (lost), "Help Rehome This {Species}" (found). Customize per method at General > Display Options > Search Card Hover Text, or per page with the new card_hover_text shortcode parameter (Junior+ tier).
upgrade_notice.8.7.0 - 8.7.2.1 (Analytics Architecture: The headline 8.7.0 release introduced a daily summary table that powers the dashboard, dwell-time impression tracking (only counts cards visitors actually see for >=500ms), and a sendBeacon-only fire-and-forget tracker so visitors no longer wait on analytics writes. Five new KB articles cover the analytics pipeline, WP-Cron requirements, and privacy. 8.7.1 adds shortcode-attribute self-healing for block builders that strip whitespace, plus standardizes 18 detail-template layouts so the social-share / instructions / print-poster trio sits directly under the main image. 8.7.2 adds automatic cron health detection. 8.7.2.1 fixes theme template overrides.
upgrade_notice.8.6.x (Shortcode Builder + Public Perfor: The 8.6 series introduced the four-phase visual Shortcode Builder (search, details, detail, option sub-tabs) under Admin > PetMatchPro Options. Each tab generates copy-paste-ready shortcodes scoped to your partner, method, license tier, and configured fields. The series also delivered a major public-side performance pass: deferred impression tracking after window.load, bulk multi-row INSERTs for analytics events (5-10x faster), defer-loaded public scripts, lazy-loaded card images, and currency-symbol fixes for £ and € worldwide. Spanish (es_ES) translation regenerated. Schema self-heals on next admin page load for sites upgrading via FTP or auto-update.
upgrade_notice.8.5.x (Detail-Page Consistency + Nameles: Title, location, and sex rendering consolidated into a shared base template. Lost-animal titles now use a consistent name-first format ("{Name} Lost in {Location}") across all three partners, with graceful fallback when location data is missing. Numeric shelter IDs (e.g., "60100465") fall back to friendly tooltip text like "This Dog" across ~40 icon, overlay, video, thumbnail, and search-card sites. PetPoint search templates now load field labels dynamically so custom labels work for every field.
upgrade_notice.8.4.x (Hide Empty Fields): New unified "hide empty fields" feature with per-method admin checkboxes (available on all license tiers) and a Junior+ shortcode parameter. Cleans up cards and detail pages when shelter data has partial records. Per-partner zero-is-empty rule for weight fields (so weight of 0 shows as "Not Defined" instead of "0 lbs").
upgrade_notice.8.1.4 / 8.0.1: Poster overlay icons on detail templates, name duplication fix, legacy settings migration, SEO Diagnostics tools, JSON-LD refactor, and translation updates.
